commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#35714: validation: return block-file flush errors

12f691cf286ea9a020583d267b94efca102a4056 validation: return block-file flush errors (Lőrinc)
07d23eb75527b8dd6571a33b3bc304815764bc07 test: characterize writes after flush failure (Lőrinc)

Pull request description:

  **Problem:** When flushing block or undo data fails, `FlushStateToDisk()` still writes block-index metadata and coins data, then advances `m_last_flushed_block`.
  With a separate `-blocksdir`, persistent failures there can leave metadata referring to block data that is not durable even when chainstate writes succeed.

  **Fix:** Return the flush error before those writes, leaving the last-flushed marker and on-disk coins tip unchanged in the failing call.
  Later flushes can retry and write if they succeed, including during shutdown.
  `ConnectTip()` and `DisconnectTip()` propagate the error before updating the chain tip, after applying the coins changes in memory.

  **History:**
  * [#27866](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/27866#discussion_r1297313148) raised whether saving other state after a flush failure was preferable. This change preserves later retries while skipping writes in the failing call.
  * [#34897](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34897) introduced `m_last_flushed_block` to prevent persistent indexes from advancing past flushed chainstate. This fix keeps it at the last successful flush.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36676: cli: respect -rpcclienttimeout even when sending

e5d9a7e04b50c723aeb65984e5048ffd098f6737 cli: fail to send a request when the socket does not become writable (Antoine Poinsot)

Pull request description:

  The move away from libevent introduced a small regression in this regard. In #36299, we switched the timeout to apply per socket wait, but continued on to another socket wait in case of timeout, instead of returning. See commit message for details.

  In general, we also shouldn't ignore `Sock::Wait`'s errors and timeouts by silently retrying forever.

  Fix these issues by returning instead when `Sock::Wait` times out or returns an error. ~~Tentative bot functional test for this in second commit that appears to be robust enough.~~

Pull request description:

  This is a follow-up to #35482.

  Add `ReachabilityGoal()` to aggregate whether selected conditions are reached across all inputs processed by a fuzz target. Goals are identified by source location and reported at shutdown. Setting `FUZZ_ENFORCE_REACHABILITY=1` makes the process fail if any registered goal was not reached.

  Add goals for selected high-value paths, including IBD and non-IBD message processing, completed P2P handshakes and transport messages, successful estimator/mempool/snapshot operations, transaction and package acceptance, and compact block reconstruction.

  ### Testing

  Built the fuzz binary and replayed the current qa-assets corpora for all instrumented targets with `FUZZ_ENFORCE_REACHABILITY=1`.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36684: test: check AddToBlockIndex keeps first-seen header on equal work

701545e5b5750aa24cfc87b2db93f4f81accb67c test: check AddToBlockIndex keeps first-seen header on equal work (Bruno Garcia)

Pull request description:

  `BlockManager::AddToBlockIndex` only replaces best_header when the new header has strictly more chain work. Add a unit test that adds two sibling headers with equal work and checks that best_header keeps pointing to the first one.

  Kills the following mutant (https://mutanthub.space/mutants/3806):
  ```diff
  diff --git a/src/node/blockstorage.cpp b/src/node/blockstorage.cpp
  index 2ee13aa417..aad52d6d61 100644
  --- a/src/node/blockstorage.cpp
  +++ b/src/node/blockstorage.cpp
  @@ -246,7 +246,7 @@ CBlockIndex* BlockManager::AddToBlockIndex(const CBlockHeader& block, CBlockInde
       pindexNew->nTimeMax = (pindexNew->pprev ? std::max(pindexNew->pprev->nTimeMax, pindexNew->nTime) : pindexNew->nTime);
       pindexNew->nChainWork = (pindexNew->pprev ? pindexNew->pprev->nChainWork : 0) + GetBlockProof(*pindexNew);
       pindexNew->RaiseValidity(BLOCK_VALID_TREE);
  -    if (best_header == nullptr || best_header->nChainWork < pindexNew->nChainWork) {
  +    if (best_header == nullptr || best_header->nChainWork <= pindexNew->nChainWork) {
           best_header = pindexNew;
       }
  ```

Require the `-rpcwait` command to wait at least the configured timeout
period before raising a process error. Measure the wait using
`time.monotonic()` so that wall-clock discrepancies do not cause
intermittent test failures.

Also, lower the timeout from 5 to 1 second.

commit.message:
cli: fail to send a request when the socket does not become writable

HTTPClient::SendRequest() waits for the socket to become writable and
went back to waiting whenever Sock::Wait() returned without SendEvent.
Before 1805716354, the `continue` was the route to the deadline check. That
commit removed the deadline, so a Sock::Wait() timeout silently started
waiting again, forever. This means -rpcclienttimeout is never respected
when sending: bitcoin-cli will hang for as long as the server keeps the
connection open without reading the request.

Fix this by returning a failure whenever `Sock::Wait()` timeouts or errors.

Merge bitcoin-core/gui#955: qt: filter addhdkey from RPC console history

31467d59a5a8e6721af1dc5d6592fad31339bcb9 qt: filter addhdkey from RPC console history (Mateusz Klatt)

Pull request description:

  Filters `addhdkey` arguments from RPC console history, consistent with other RPCs that handle private key material.

  This prevents extended private keys from being retained in history. It also covers the mnemonic and passphrase inputs proposed in bitcoin/bitcoin#35857.

  Adds a parser test verifying that the arguments are redacted.

  ## Motivation

  `addhdkey` accepts a BIP 32 extended private key, but its arguments are currently retained in RPC console history, unlike other RPCs that handle private key material.

  The same filter would also protect the mnemonic and passphrase inputs proposed in bitcoin/bitcoin#35857.

  ## Changes

  - Add `addhdkey` to the RPC console sensitive-command filter.
  - Add a parser test verifying that its arguments are redacted as `addhdkey(…)`.

  ## Tests

  - `./build_gui/bin/test_bitcoin-qt` — all tests passed, including `RPCNestedTests::rpcNestedTests()`.
